question_type: two-observation weekly log-return volatility from a pinned issue (10/1960): extract two 26-week bill discount rates one week apart from an OCR-garbled narrative table (dates merged, one row dropped), cross-check with the Public Debt Operations offerings table, then apply a stated but convention-sensitive formula (annualization factor)
decisive_step: Two decisions. (i) Extraction: the narrative table at treasury_bulletin_1960_10.txt:244-249 merges 'Sept. 1' and '8' into one date cell and drops the Sept 15 row, so the date labels cannot be trusted; the reference anchored the two 26-week rates in Table 2 'Offerings of Treasury Bills (Continued)', column 'Equivalent average rate', second element of each '13-week 26-week' pair on the 'Sept. 1p.' and 'Sept. 8p.' rows (worklog Step 4; reference corpus lines 1943-1944, which are lines 1945-1946 in the v9 corpus copy). All three cells and the reference made this identically. (ii) Convention: one log return, realized variance = its square, annualized with 52 weekly periods (worklog Step 5; calc.py). The reference notes that 365/7 periods or a simple return each move the result by a few tenths of a percent relative. Every cell and the reference used log return x 52 and all were graded wrong with error_bin within_1pct, so the grader's key follows one of the other conventions; this convention choice is the step that separates right from wrong and nobody had evidence for it.

a.path_summary: find_tables on the question's nouns ([5]-[9]) did not surface the 1960_10 narrative table (it is untitled in that issue); rg on the issue ([13]) found the narrative line and the table at line 244; show_table --long --raw ([17]) printed the four garbled rows with no repair flag. It recognised the merged/missing dates ([16],[18]) and resolved them by grepping the rate values, which hit the Table 2 rows for Sept 1 and Sept 8 ([19]-[20]). Computed sqrt(52 * r^2) x 100 with calc ([22]) and answered as a percent ([24]).

first_divergence.what_it_did: Chose the annualization convention 'weekly -> 52 periods' with a log return, exactly as the reference did ('Annualized volatility = sqrt(52 * r^2)'); extraction, formula and rounding all match the reference, which was itself graded wrong.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: No cell or reference was right. The reference's sensitivity list (worklog Step 5) shows the key must use another convention within 1% (365/7 periods per year, or a simple rather than log change); none of the materials say which.

smallest_change.change: No adapter change is supported by the evidence: all three cells reproduced the reference's extraction (two 26-week rates for Sept 1 and Sept 8, cross-anchored in Table 2) and the reference's formula (single log return, squared, x 52, square root, percent, 2 decimals), and the reference itself is graded wrong with every answer within 1% of the key. The key evidently follows a different annualization/return convention (the reference's Step 5 sensitivity list names 365/7 periods per year and simple-return as the two nearby alternatives); no document in the corpus and no line of text could tell a model which one the question writer used.

alternatives.change: Conventions line: 'Annualizing weekly data: if the question says "weekly" and gives no day count, use 52 periods per year; if it gives dates one week apart, 365/7.' (or the reverse) - a guess at the key's convention.
alternatives.why_not_first: Pure speculation about the grader; a wrong guess would flip other volatility questions that today pass with 52. Would need the answer key to calibrate, which is off limits.

alternatives.change: Harness hygiene (does not fix this question, removes ~22 wasted steps in b): (1) flagged_cells should bind a calc literal to the cell the model itself printed most recently, or to a cell in the issue the question pins, before falling back to any other issue - here it bound to treasury_bulletin_1961_01.txt:1852 although the model's evidence was 1960_10; (2) table_alternatives must not fire when the 'other' table is another part or '(Continued)' page of the table already used (same title stem in the same issue); (3) a --keep submit should be recorded rather than answered with a fresh finding of a different rule when the answer is unchanged.
alternatives.why_not_first: Would not change correctness here; listed for the v10 controls decision.

alternatives.change: printings/show_table: split '13-week 26-week' paired cells (two numbers in one cell) into two sub-columns labelled by the header's series names, so printings --col 'Equivalent average rate' --series 26-week returns the second element; today printings returns only the first number of the pair (b[41]-[42]). And show_table should flag a narrative table whose stub cells contain two day numbers ('Sept. 18' where the text says five issues) as SUSPECT-DATES.
alternatives.why_not_first: Cells worked around both by reading Table 2 raw; useful friction reduction, not a fix.

fix.irreducible: Yes. The reference solution (graded 0), all three v9 cells and all three v8 arms produced the same value with the same convention; error_bin is within_1pct everywhere. This is a convention-of-the-key question (annualization factor or return type), not an adapter failure; treat it as a disputed reference for learner scoring even though issue47 is false.

notes: 1) The narrative table in 1960_10 (line 244) is a trap the tools do not flag: OCR merged 'Sept. 1' and '8' into one stub cell and dropped a row, so its date labels are shifted by one row; all cells noticed it by reasoning ('five issues but four rows') and recovered via Table 2. show_table printed it as '(untitled)' with no repair flag, and find_tables cannot reach it by the sentence that introduces it. 2) Table 2's 'Equivalent average rate' cells hold two numbers ('13-week 26-week'); printings returns only the first, silently giving the wrong series (b[41]-[42]); show_table --raw is the only way to see both. 3) b's two gate findings were both false alarms (literal bound to a later issue's repaired row; 'alternative table' = part 1 of the same table) and consumed 2 of 2 gate rounds; a --keep did not record the answer but triggered a second, different finding. 4) For the learner: since the reference and every arm agree and are graded wrong, this question gives no signal about adapter quality; exclude it from fitness or mark it as disputed.
